# Local Git checkpoints

Use this shared capability only when a coordinator identifies a meaningful checkpoint in the actual consumer project. It is not a new RPIR phase, a Git automation service, or proof of runtime compliance. Follow the [checkpoint checklist](references/checkpoint-checklist.md); it owns the portable applicability, grant, preservation, execution and reporting procedure.

Every prospective Plan must include one explicit bounded local staging/append-only strategy. Every detailed Work Item references it and states its normal post-validation checkpoint boundary, coherent content and purpose, or a specific justified combination, deferral or no-commit exception. Each exception states the actual constraint/reason, affected IDs, validation/dependency consequence, later boundary if one exists and why the normal boundary is unsuitable. Unknown future obstacles must not be invented. Empty headings, generic exemptions and unexplained blanket bans fail planning assessment; an actual prohibition still grants no Git authority, including in historical Plans. Use the existing hierarchy, not a second register or repeated Git procedures.

Coordinators propose eligible coherent content based on the approved outcome, actual saved/read-back evidence and local versioning policy. Normally checkpoint eligible validated Work Items before unrelated work and proactively consider earlier coherent validated Tasks, without artificial splitting or a session-end-sweep default. At every expected boundary, Implement records planned-versus-actual disposition evidence before unrelated work: a verified checkpoint or a specific supported combination/deferral/no-commit or runtime outcome under checklist §6. Runtime obstacles belong in fresh implementation evidence, not retrospective substantive Plan exceptions. Review and assurance assess omissions and reasons, not commit count as technical acceptance.

An engineer's explicit approval of an inspected Plan that states the bounded local staging/append-only commit strategy authorizes only those covered effects after the explicit `/implement` transition; no second grant exchange is required for unchanged covered effects. The Plan is the authorization reference, not a concrete candidate: it may approve the strategy before a candidate exists. A silent, prohibiting, or unapproved-option Plan supplies no authority. The coordinator binds that inspected Plan/version and actual approval/invocation evidence, literal candidate and validation evidence to one goal-directed Script Runner invocation. Runner inspects runtime facts and returns observed effects; it cannot invent authority or candidate scope, author files/records, update Plan markers, clean up, approve scope, accept work or hand off phases. Revocation or materially changed effects require resolution; runtime identity, state, validation, helper and permission checks still apply.

A verified non-Git/other-VCS project or no eligible change is a normal skip: do not initialize Git, prompt repeatedly, or block independent RPIR work, record persistence, validation or manual handoff. Missing/inaccessible Git or uncertain repository membership is unavailable/unresolved, not a fabricated skip. Ignore and explicit local exclusions apply to all work; never force-add or alter them. A checkpoint neither advances a phase nor establishes validation or Review acceptance.

Separately authorized phase-record checkpoints retain their bounded route under checklist §3: an explicit engineer grant may cover an eligible saved/read-back Research brief, working Plan or Review report without an approved implementation Plan or `/implement` evidence. Supply that grant instead of Plan authority, with the same literal candidate, validation, ownership, helper and permission safeguards. This does not require another grant for unchanged Plan-covered effects, override a prohibition, or authorize source edits.

This Skill grants no tools, permissions, Git effects or lifecycle authority. Static guidance and checks do not establish consumer configuration, platform permission, installation or agent behavior.
